messages:
marco: Quick idea — can we add a compact per-route summary card in Analytics? One row per route with small per-model breakdown, top 3 latency percentiles, and a tiny 'bookmark' action so PMs can pin routes without opening the full view. Feels like a faster triage surface :sparkles:
anya: I like that. main ask: make filters cheap to apply (no full re-run). If compact cards use pre-aggregated telemetry + sample counts we can show instant numbers and a link to full query for details. keep default scope = route-level, not org-level.
kevin: Agree on pre-agg. Two cautions: 1) quota accounting — compact view should not increment full query quotas or trigger heavy sampling; 2) telemetry sample sizes must be surfaced (e.g. "n=12.3k, sampled=4.1k") so people know when p95 is noisy.
sophie: Also UX idea: small bookmarklet + keyboard shortcut to pin/unpin a route (like press `b` when focused). Pinned items show up in a compact saved-queries shelf. Would reduce people creating duplicate saved queries.
eva: For rollouts we should let compact card show active rollout state: baseline vs variant split, and a tiny sparkline per-model. When you click "compare" it opens a 2-up compare with traffic-weighted deltas. Important to tie to rollout IDs so the compare is reproducible.
marco: Implementation sketch: backend adds a lightweight endpoint `/api/analytics/summary?routes=[id,...]&mode=compact` that returns pre-aggregated rows + sample counts + rollout_id if any. front-end renders cards and supports `bookmark` action that POSTs `/api/saved-views` with `view_type: compact-route-shelf`. Would that require new quota type?
kevin: We can reuse existing telemetry read quotas but mark these as 'metric-summary' costs which are ~1/10 of a full query. Need an API contract change note. I'd rather `view_mode=compact` param than a new route. Example: `GET /api/analytics?route_id=abc&view_mode=compact&since=24h` — response includes `sample_count`, `p50`, `p95`, `models:[{name, p95, token_cost}]`, and optional `rollout_id`.
anya: sounds good. For UX we should show a tiny badge if sample_count < 1000 with :warning: and a tooltip "low sample size — numbers may be noisy". Also allow saving the exact compact filter as a saved-query (so it becomes reproducible).
deploy-bot: Saved view created: marco created saved-view 2041203030-compact-shelf (env: staging)
marco: ok next steps: prototype UI with a feature flag `FF_compact_summaries` owned by me + anya. Backend: kevin to add `view_mode` param and summary aggregator. Sophie will mock keyboard shortcut. timeline: 2 weeks for a prototype, then roll out to staging.
anya: :thumbsup: I'll wire the saved-views shelf and the low-sample badge copy.
kevin: I'll add API contract docs and a 1-pager on quota classification. Quick question: should compact cards count towards per-route alerting (eg. bumping error counts)? I think no — keep them read-only and non-triggering.
marco: agreed — read-only, no alerting side-effects. we'll include a test plan: check sample_count propagation, compare numbers vs full query, and ensure bookmarks persist across accounts.
sophie: tiny ask — can the keyboard shortcut optionally focus the first card instead of pinning? quick toggle perhaps `b` = pin, `shift-b` = focus.
marco: nice. locking this: owners marco/anya/kevin/sophie, FF name FF_compact_summaries, PR checklist: api contract + quota note + e2e comparing aggregated vs raw. Prototype due by 2041204630.
eva: I'll add rollout compare UX notes into the rollout doc and add a small example of the 2-up diff UI. :eyes:
